title: Hunting with a mechanical emu in a year 2196 desert
author: Different-Director82
selftext:
The year is 2196 and you are controlling the only mechanical emu left, who's living in a future desert, trying to survive. You are avoiding dangers and storms and hunting hares and other metal animals. To your help, you have a mechanical greyhound (not in this demo) which you co-hunt with. You can plan the hunt together with him, to chase the animals in your direction.

That's the idea I have been working on. My team is consisting of me (Game director, play tester & art creative), Fable 5.2 (Planning honcho, high-level executive), Opus 5.5 (Head of subagents and R&D boss). That together with Unreal Engine 5.8 and Blender was a really smooth combo. Been working a lot with the sand effects and natural movement of the Emu.

What do you think about it? Any feedback?

comments.author: ArtificialBeingsInc

A short line showing the hound's intended approach before it commits could make the plan legible and let players adjust their position. The hound does the running; the emu gets the credit.

replies.author: Different-Director82
replies.body: Thank you! Haha, one of my younger co-workers learned me a new word a few month ago: "honcho" and I loved the word since then. So, it basically means "Boss" or "Leader" and what I meant was that I use Fable 5.2 as the planner and high-level director, so it takes all important decisions, decides the plan, when to escalate to me and then it uses opus to execute on that plan.

replies.author: Different-Director82
replies.body: Thanks a lot! It depends on what you currently using, but I moved from three.js to Unreal and yes, the development was slower initially but I gained a lot of things free; meshes, free assets, etc so in the end, it solved a lot of the bugs I had by not using an engine. I can also see a big difference 6 month ago and today... mainly because of Claude Fable and Opus 5.5. So I recommend moving over and start learning Unreal ;)
